input.question: What position does Comte de Digoine currently or formerly hold?

documents.text: As the sun set over the bustling streets of Melbourne, a peculiar figure emerged from the crowd. Comte de Digoine, resplendent in his tailcoat and top hat, cut a dashing figure as he made his way to the Australian Parliament House. The year was 1885, and the Comte, a French aristocrat, had found himself in the unlikeliest of positions - a member of the Australian House of Representatives. It was a chilly autumn evening, and the gas lamps that lined the streets cast a warm, golden glow over the scene. The Comte, his bushy mustache twirled to perfection, nodded to the passersby as he strode purposefully towards the parliament building. His eyes, a piercing blue, twinkled with a hint of mischief, a trait that had served him well in his previous life as a diplomat in the French Foreign Service. As he entered the grand hall, the Comte was greeted by the familiar sight of his fellow representatives, busily engaged in heated debates and whispered conversations. He exchanged a warm smile with the Speaker of the House, a gruff but fair-minded man named Sir Malcolm Fraser, before taking his seat on the government benches. The Comte's presence in the Australian parliament was a curiosity, to say the least. Few could have predicted that a French aristocrat, with a reputation for wit and cunning, would find himself representing the interests of the people of Melbourne North. And yet, here he was, a testament to the power of circumstance and the Comte's own irrepressible charm. As the evening wore on, the Comte listened intently to the debates, his eyes darting between the speakers as he weighed the merits of each argument. His thoughts, however, were elsewhere, drifting back to the events that had brought him to this unlikely position. The whispers of scandal, the hasty departure from Paris, the chance encounter with a charismatic Australian politician... it was a story for another time, one that the Comte would keep close to his chest for now. For the moment, he was content to bask in the glow of his newfound status, to soak up the atmosphere of this strange and wonderful place. As the clock struck nine, the Comte rose from his seat, his voice booming through the chamber as he addressed his fellow representatives.
